items.prompt: Now White's seventh move was the queen to d2 instead of the pawn to f3. Black to move. If the knight jumps to g4, can White win it?

claims.statement: After ...Ng4 no white piece attacks the knight on g4.
...Ng4 is the engine's top move here (depth 16).

hints: Count the white pieces that look at g4 after the jump. Which squares do the queen on d2 and the bishop on e3 attack?
The queen sees d2-e3 and the h6 diagonal, not g4. The pawn that could have guarded g4 stands on f2.
No white piece attacks g4, so the knight is safe there.
items.explain: No white piece attacks g4 once the knight lands there, and the engine rates the jump as Black's best move. Without the pawn on f3 the square g4 is free for Black's knight.

items.prompt: White's seventh move was the bishop to e2 this time. Black to move. Is the square g4 guarded by a white piece?

claims.statement: One white piece (the bishop on e2) attacks g4.

hints: Look along the diagonal from e2 towards the h5 corner. What stands between e2 and g4?
f3 is empty, so the bishop on e2 sees f3 and g4.
Yes: the bishop on e2 guards g4.
items.explain: The bishop on e2 attacks g4 through the empty square f3, so a knight on g4 can be taken.

items.prompt: Edited position: the white pawn stands on f2. Tap every square the pawn on f2 guards.

claims.statement: The pawn on f2 attacks exactly e3 and g3.

hints: A pawn guards the two squares diagonally in front of it.
White pawns move up the board. In front of f2 are the files e and g.
e3 and g3.
items.explain: A white pawn guards the two squares diagonally ahead of it. From f2 that is e3 and g3. After f3 those two squares lose their pawn guard.

items.prompt: White to move. Find a move that starts the pawn storm.

claims.statement: A pawn on g4 would be guarded by the pawn on f3.
g4 is one of the engine's four best moves (depth 16).

hints: Which of the four moves lands on a square the pawn on f3 attacks?
A pawn attacks the two squares diagonally in front of it: e4 and g4.
The move g2-g4.
items.explain: A white pawn arriving on g4 is guarded by the pawn on f3, which attacks g4 and e4. The engine rates g4 among White's four best moves here.

items.prompt: White to move. Is the bishop trade on h6 (bishop e3 to h6) a good idea in this exact position?

claims.statement: At depth 16, e3-h6 loses at least three pawns in this position.

hints: Who defends the knight on d4 right now, and who attacks it?
The bishop on e3 and the queen on d2 defend d4. If the bishop goes to h6 and is traded, what is left?
After the trade nothing defends the knight on d4, and the knight on c6 attacks it.
items.explain: The bishop on e3 is one of d4's two defenders. After the bishop is taken on h6 and the queen retakes, nothing defends d4 and the knight on c6 wins the knight. A plan needs its conditions checked first.

feedback_by_move.e3h6: The engine at depth 16 rates this as losing at least three pawns: the knight on d4 loses its bishop and queen as defenders.
feedback_by_move.g2g4: Not what the question asks: g4 is a strong move here, but it is not a bishop trade on h6.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's knight is still on b8, not on c6. Is the bishop trade on h6 playable here, losing no material?

claims.statement: The trade on h6 loses no material (bishop for bishop).
No black piece attacks the knight on d4.

hints: Who attacks the knight on d4 in this position?
Black's knight is still on b8, so nothing attacks d4; the bishop is free to leave.
Yes: the trade loses no material.
items.explain: With Black's knight still on b8 nothing attacks d4, so the bishop can leave its guard post and the trade loses no material. The engine still prefers long castling or g4, but the trade is playable. Compare the same position with the knight on c6.

items.prompt: White to move (Black has just castled). Find White's best move.

claims.statement: Qd2 is the engine's top move here (depth 16).
Castling long is illegal now: the queen still stands on d1.

hints: White cannot castle long yet. Which piece stands between king and rook?
The queen on d1. Which developing move frees d1 and guards the bishop on e3?
The queen to d2.
items.explain: Long castling is illegal while the queen stands on d1. The queen to d2 clears d1, guards the bishop on e3 and, later, prepares the trade on h6. The engine ranks it first (depth 16).

feedback_by_move.g2g4: A good move too, but it does not clear d1 yet, so long castling stays impossible.
feedback_by_move.f1c4: Playable, but it does not yet prepare long castling.

items.prompt: Black to move. Tap every square the rook on a8 can reach right now.

claims.statement: The rook on a8 can only go to b8: the bishop on c8 blocks the way.

hints: Look at the squares next to the rook along the back rank.
b8 is empty. What stands on c8?
Only b8.
items.explain: The bishop on c8 blocks the rook. That is why Black's next job is the bishop: it has to leave c8 before a rook can use the c-file.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's ninth move was the bishop to e2. Is the freeing break ...d5 a good move for Black here?

claims.statement: ...d5 and ...Nxd4 are the engine's two best moves, within 0.4 pawns (depth 16).

hints: Count who controls d5: Black's knight and queen against which white pieces?
With the bishop on e2 (not c4), only the knight on c3 and the pawn on e4 attack d5.
Yes: d5 is among the engine's best two moves.
items.explain: With the bishop on e2 only the knight on c3 and the pawn on e4 control d5, so the break works. The engine names ...d5 and ...Nxd4 as Black's two best moves (depth 16).

items.prompt: Black to move. White's ninth move was the bishop to c4. Is the freeing break ...d5 a good move for Black here?

claims.statement: At depth 16 ...d5 costs Black at least 0.3 pawns here.

hints: Count again: who controls d5 now?
The bishop on c4, the knight on c3 and the pawn on e4 attack d5; Black has two defenders.
No: d5 costs ground.
items.explain: With the bishop on c4 three white pieces attack d5 against two defenders, and the engine says the break costs Black at least 0.3 pawns (depth 16).

items.prompt: Black to move. White's ninth move was the pawn to a3, a slow move far from d5. Is ...d5 a good move for Black?

claims.statement: ...d5 is the engine's top move (depth 16).

hints: Does a3 change who controls d5?
The bishop is still on f1, so d5 is controlled by the knight and the pawn only.
Yes: d5 works. The pawn on a3 is irrelevant to d5.
items.explain: The pawn on a3 does nothing for d5, and the bishop is still on f1, so ...d5 works. The engine ranks it first (depth 16).

items.prompt: The queen has just taken on g4. Can the bishop on d7 take the queen?

claims.statement: The move Bd7xg4 is illegal: the bishop is pinned to the king by the bishop on b5.

hints: Which white piece gave check a moment ago?
The bishop on b5 attacks d7 and the king on e8 stands behind it on the same diagonal.
No: the bishop on d7 is pinned.
items.explain: The bishop on b5 pins the bishop on d7 to the king on e8, so d7-g4 is illegal. That is why the queen can take on g4 for free, and why the queen moving to d2 first changes this tactic.

items.prompt: White to move in the Yugoslav position. Find a good move (three are within half a pawn of the best). Several tempting moves are mistakes; the feedback tells you why.

claims.statement: Long castling is the engine's first choice; Bc4 and g4 are within half a pawn of it (depth 16).
e3-h6 loses at least three pawns (depth 16).
a2-a3 costs at least half a pawn (depth 16).
f1-d3 costs at least 0.6 pawns (depth 16).

hints: Which moves use f3, the queen on d2 or the empty squares to the left of the king?
Think of a pawn push that f3 now protects, and of castling.
g2-g4 or castling long.
items.explain: Long castling is the engine's first choice (roughly +0.5 to +0.9, varying by run); the bishop to c4 and the pawn push g4 (protected by f3) are within half a pawn of it. The bishop trade on h6 loses the knight on d4's guards; a3 and the bishop to d3 let ...d5 equalise.

feedback_by_move.e3h6: The bishop is one of the two defenders of the knight on d4. After the trade on h6 the knight on c6 wins the knight on d4.
feedback_by_move.a2a3: A slow move far from the action: it does not stop ...d5, which the engine rates as Black's best reply. It costs at least half a pawn.
feedback_by_move.f1d3: The bishop on d3 does not stop ...d5 and blocks the d-file for the rook that is about to arrive. It costs at least 0.6 pawns.

items.prompt: Black to move after the bishop went to c4. Find a good move (three are within 0.4 pawns). Two natural-looking moves are mistakes.

claims.statement: Qa5, Bd7 and Nxd4 are the engine's top three moves (depth 16, within 0.4 pawns).
a7-a6 costs at least a quarter of a pawn (depth 16).
d6-d5 costs at least 0.3 pawns (depth 16).
f6xe4 loses at least three pawns (depth 16).

hints: Which black pieces are still undeveloped? Which move uses the half-open c-file or the long diagonal?
Think of moves that develop or trade, not of pawn moves.
The queen to a5, the bishop to d7, or the knight takes on d4.
items.explain: Qa5, Bd7 and Nxd4 are Black's top three at depth 16. Masters chose Bd7 in 116 of the games from this position and the trade on d4 in 25 (our data). The early ...a6 and the break ...d5 each cost ground.

feedback_by_move.a7a6: Slow: it does not develop and White gains tempo for the pawn storm (engine: costs at least a quarter of a pawn). Masters did choose it 10 times; the engine disagrees. [V] counts, not a verdict.
feedback_by_move.d6d5: With the bishop on c4 the break fails: three white pieces attack d5 and Black has two defenders.
feedback_by_move.f6e4: The knight takes a pawn defended by f3 and the knight on c3, and it loses a piece.
